newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway operators set up joint deepwater programme.
newsitem.headline: Norway operators set up joint deepwater programme.

text.p: Four development projects have been launched under a programme set up a year ago by operators of deepwater acreage awarded in Norway's 15th offshore licencing round, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Thursday.

The five-year programme has a budget of 45 million crowns ($6.9 million) for 1997, spread over seven licences. In 1996, 20 million crowns was committed to the programme, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.

"We proposed this deepwater programme to create a forum for all the operators to tackle collectively the technological challenges presented by future exploration and development in the Norwegian Sea," Stein Thorbjoernsen, head of Statoil's Vema/Nyk project.

Norske Shell AS heads a project to collect regional meteorological and oceanographic data, while Norsk Hydro ASA is using high-resolution seismic data and other methods to gain a better understanding of the seabed in the area.

British Petroleum is looking at the development of appropriate risers -- tubes transporting crude from the seabed to the surface -- and mooring systems for rough conditions and deep water. Statoil's project focuses on deepwater subsea installations.
Statoil said a technical committee had been established for each of the four projects with specialists from all companies involved, to provide advice and transfer of experience.
